// era-position.js.txt — SCANNED, NEVER RUN. THE POSITIONAL FEATURE, and it is
// a file of its own for a reason worth stating: `era.js.txt` is asserted to
// fail es2020 for EXACTLY ONE reason, and that reason is an OPERATOR. Putting a
// top-level await in it would have made that assertion two-valued and quietly
// destroyed what it demonstrates — that `attr_needs` sees a feature no
// kind-level table can.
//
// Both awaits below are `await_expression` with identical attributes. The first
// is ES2022 and the second is ES2017, and the only difference is what is ABOVE
// them. That is the whole subject of `outside_attr_needs`.
const early = await Promise.resolve(1);

async function later(url) {
  return await Promise.resolve(url);
}

export { early, later };
